title: SLO-Gradient Autoscaler and Burst Handshake — PRD Draft
body:
Purpose:
This doc sketches a new autoscaling model (SLO-Gradient Autoscaler) plus a burst handshake protocol for Dedicated pools. Goal: let tenants safely consume burst capacity while preserving latency SLOs for critical tenants and providing a predictable fallback path to hosted variants when isolation constraints or capacity limits are hit.

Problem statement / motivation:
- Current binary autoscale (grow/shrink) produces sudden shifts in latency for noisy tenants and can force broad throttles.
- Many customers want predictable soft-bursting but don’t want full pre-reservation or hard evictions.
- We need a coordinated, observable handoff between Dedicated pools and Hosted fallback to avoid user-visible failures when Dedicated is saturated.

Core ideas (TL;DR):
1) SLO-Gradient Autoscaler: scale decisions are based on a continuous risk score that blends token-latency percentiles, queue depth, and recent error-rate. Instead of single thresholds, we maintain a gradient (0..1) per tenant/pool that maps to scaling aggressiveness.
2) Burst Handshake Protocol: when gradient approaches maximum and we can’t allocate more capacity immediately, we initiate a timed handshake to move a subset of requests to pre-negotiated hosted-compatible model variants. Handshake includes tokenized proofs (burst-handshake tokens) and a brief transition window with traffic shadowing/validation.
3) Tenant Isolation Controls: introduce "sandbox leases" (transient soft-isolation) and "circuit tokens" to limit noisy neighbor impact. Sandboxes give tenants temporary CPU/GPU headroom at reduced fidelity with guarantees on reclaim windows.

Detailed design:
- Inputs for SLO-Gradient:
  - p50/p95/p99 generation latencies over 1/5/15m windows
  - queue length (requests waiting to be batched)
  - model-level slowdowns (kernel stalls)
  - error and retry fraction
  - tenant priority weight (customer tier)
- Risk score computation: weighted sum normalized to [0,1]. Tunable weights per pool.
- Mapping: gradient -> scale action
  - 0.0-0.3: no action (stable)
  - 0.3-0.6: conservative warming (prewarm one node slot, enable KV-cache sharing)
  - 0.6-0.85: aggressive prewarm + soft-sandbox eligible for high-risk tenants
  - >0.85: handshake window start (30s default)
- Handshake sequence (when >0.85 and no immediate capacity):
  1) Coordinator emits handshake-intent to tenant runtime (10s TTL).
  2) Tenant may accept: system mints a burst-handshake token (short-lived JWT) scoped to the model family and fallback route.
  3) Gateway begins mirrored traffic to hosted variant (shadow for 5s) to validate fidelity and latency.
  4) If shadow pass meets fidelity thresholds, route X% of traffic to hosted route and issue temporary sandbox lease to reduce Dedicated resource pressure.
  5) If token not accepted or validation fails, system initiates throttle plan with SLA notice to customer.
- Sandbox leases: 1–5 minute soft leases that lower fidelity (quantize, reduce generation length, beam changes) and mark requests with a special header for downstream observability. Leases are cancellable and have a renewable counter.

Isolation controls and policies:
- Circuit tokens: per-tenant token limiting concurrent burst-handshakes. Default concurrency 1; enterprise customers may request higher.
- Priority preemption: define three buckets (critical, standard, economizer). When capacity constrained, economizer traffic is first suggested for handshake/fidelity reduction.
- Fairness knob: ceiling on per-tenant share of burst capacity over rolling window (e.g., 20% of pool tokens over 1h).

Observability / metrics:
- Per-tenant gradient time-series, handshake attempts, handshake success ratio, fallback latency delta, sandboxed request fraction, fidelity-regression rate (automated evals).
- New dashboard tile: "handshake health" showing active handshakes, failures, and reasons.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (lab): offline simulator on historical traces; tune weights and default windows (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (canary): opt-in beta for 3 internal customers and 2 low-risk external tenants. Shadow-only (no live traffic shifting) + alerting. (4 weeks)
- Phase 2 (soft-launch): enable handshake with small % routing to hosted (5-10%) for consenting tenants. Expose sandbox controls in Console. (6 weeks)
- Phase 3 (general availability): default behavior with conservative limits and enterprise toggles.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- No more than 1% increase in p99 for critical-tier tenants in canary pools during Phase 1.
- Handshake success rate >= 95% in Phase 2 for consenting tenants.
- Operator TTL to remediate handshake failures < 10m in initial launch.
- Clear billing traceability for hosted-fallback tokens.

Operational runbook highlights (rough):
- Handshake failure modes: token auth failure, fidelity regression, no hosted capacity. Each should map to automated rollback actions and a triage label.
- Emergency kill: operator can revoke all handshake tokens for a pool and force immediate sandbox reclamation.
- Audit logs: handshake actions should be auditable per-request for compliance.

Open questions / risks:
- Customer acceptance: will some customers reject any fallback to hosted? Need per-tenant opt-out and explicit SLAs.
- Pricing/tokens: how to bill for guest-hosted compute used during handshake? Pre-bill credits vs post-bill.
- Fidelity calibration: how to define automated fidelity checks that are model-agnostic (text loss vs injection tests).
- Security: ensure handshake tokens cannot be replayed across tenants or model families.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Sim team: build trace simulator and run 2 months of production traces through gradient model (owner: Ravi).
- Infra: prototype handshake token flow and hosted routing shim (owner: Clara).
- Product: draft Console UI for sandbox lease override and visibility (owner: Maya).
- Legal/Billing: define provisional pricing calc for fallback compute (owner: Jonas).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on automation; we prefer explicit opt-ins initially.
- Looking for feedback on gradient mapping bands and handshake windows.
- If agreed, will create follow-up RFC with data model and API wireframes.

Patchy brainstorming bits below (notes-to-self):
- Consider a "cooldown credit" analogous to burst_tokens that decays over time (encourage steady behavior).
- Could leverage existing rollout/traffic-splitting infra for the % routing step.
- Need a fast way to simulate fidelity regression using prompt-set diffs.

End of draft.
